details:
ASTRAL-MED: Intelligent Health Monitoring for Astronauts on Space Missions

ASTRAL-MED is a space-health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut health and well-being during long-duration space missions. Developed in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project focuses on making astronaut health information easier to monitor, understand, and interpret through a centralised digital dashboard.

Space environments expose astronauts to several health challenges, including changes in cardiovascular function, sleep patterns, stress levels, and muscle and bone health. Continuous observation of these health indicators is important for identifying potential concerns and supporting informed decisions during missions, especially when astronauts are far from Earth.

ASTRAL-MED aims to address this challenge through an interactive web-based monitoring interface. It brings health-related information together in a visual dashboard, allowing users to view important indicators and understand changes in an astronaut's health status. Its space-inspired interface is designed to make complex information accessible through visual elements, organised data panels, and monitoring displays.

The platform is designed around the idea of continuous health awareness, early identification of unusual changes, and improved access to astronaut health information. It also provides a foundation for future integration with real-time wearable sensors, advanced data analysis, intelligent anomaly detection, and communication systems for mission support.

By combining web technology, health-data visualisation, and a space-mission-focused approach, ASTRAL-MED explores how digital monitoring tools could contribute to astronaut healthcare and safer human space exploration.

Our Vision: To make astronaut health monitoring more accessible, intelligent, and reliable, supporting the future of long-duration human space missions.

Project Website: https://astra-med-eight.vercel.app/
